nodes.title: Consistence Lora
widgets_values:
Occasionally, you may want to apply the consistency LoRA to preserve the character's appearance that already exists in the image. This is particularly useful when positioning the reference character alongside another character. 
For example: "The person in the image is taking a selfie with refchar." 
A strength setting of 0.25–0.3 typically yields good results. Additionally, set the fusion mode to "Composition Priority" or "Balanced." 

If you're only replacing the head, set the strength to 0 and change the fusion mode to "Identity Priority."

https://civitai.com/models/1939453?modelVersionId=2634354

nodes.title: refchar
widgets_values: You can name your reference character whatever you'd like in the upper field, but make sure to use that same name in your prompt.
This is the primary image that will be edited.

Load your images here. After the images have been loaded for the first time and the model has run, they will be populated into the Olm Drag Crop nodes. Stop the image generation and crop each image using the yellow boxes, making sure to lock the aspect ratio to 1:1. This step only needs to be completed once — your cropped images can be reused until new images are loaded. Finally, review the grid preview to confirm that all faces are cropped correctly, with no distortion or warping. Note that the yellow box must be applied to every newly loaded image before the crop can take effect.

The reference node requires manual installation:
https://github.com/MrWeazelHead/ComfyUI-MrWeazNodes
